description: Dark stone terraced in bands, a seam of live gold running the length of them. It lights whatever pouch you put it in.
lore: The smiths' rule with this one: never on the bench after dark. The seam is live, and beside heated metal there is no telling the colour of the work from the colour coming off the stone, so settings happen at noon with the doors open, by people who otherwise keep their doors shut to read the heat.

It does not go down when you put it away, which is why you cannot carry one and also arrive anywhere unannounced — and why, when the fire on the east road lapsed, its last keeper left a banded stone glowing on the sill as she went, so the road would think the light was still kept. [[characters/7a779de1|Wendell]] walked that road while the trick still worked. He says you could tell a mile off, because a fire moves and a stone only glows. He stopped anyway, both ways, sat down on the step, and told it what he had seen on the road lately. It seemed wrong to pass a kept light without paying for it.

What bothers people is that it lends the whole light, undiminished, out of a lump a hand closes around. As if [[monsters/night_beast|the creature it comes off]] was never lit through at all — as if the light was always this small, and the body was built around it for carrying.
